question: SQ-LIP-000036
text: Is lipedema onset influenced by heredity and family history?
minor_problems: [minor] set: No proposition states the overall conclusion that a heritable component to lipedema is accepted (E1 Delphi consensus, E21/E26 genetic basis); E1 appears only as context under P1.
[minor] set: Primary onset data (E15, E9, E7, E14, E11) are not placed under P6, which cites only narrative reviews.
[minor] set: Mild tension between P2 (Mendelian autosomal dominant models) and P4/P3 (modest polygenic contribution, heterogeneity); the wording acknowledges both but does not reconcile them.

[minor] P3: not fully supported; overgeneralized; misplaced ['E24', 'E12'] — suggested: Lipedema may be genetically heterogeneous, with candidate variants differing between affected families and no single shared causal gene identified. (Rests on one small exome study (E19) plus its editorial; E24 (AKR1C1 family) and E12 (PIT1 in a sporadic case) also point to different genes in different families and could support it. Hedged with 'may', so minor.)

[minor] P7: not fully supported; overgeneralized; two ideas; stance errors ['E4']; misplaced ['E4', 'E3'] — suggested: Altered estrogen signalling in adipose tissue, including an imbalanced estrogen receptor pattern, is proposed as a lipedema mechanism and a possible link to heritable predisposition. (Local aromatase activity appears in no finding placed here (it is in E22/E26, not listed); E4 and E3 state generic hormonal dysregulation, not receptor or aromatase mechanism, so they only partly support. E6, E17, E22, E26 describe the receptor/aromatase mechanism and should be placed here. Also only loosely about heredity.)

[minor] P8: not fully supported; overgeneralized — suggested: Hormonal contraceptive use has been anecdotally linked to worsened lipedema symptoms, on very limited evidence. (Single case report generalised to 'some women'; family history mention is not tied to this claim. Off-topic for heredity.)

propositions.statement: Genome-wide studies suggest common genetic variants may contribute modestly to lipedema susceptibility.
propositions.rationale: One biobank GWAS on an inferred phenotype with low SNP heritability and one clinical-cohort GWAS with a suggestive replicated locus; hence 'modest'.

evidence.finding: UK Biobank GWAS of an inferred lipedema phenotype: 18 genome-wide significant loci (RSPO3, GRB14-COBLL1, VEGFA, ADAMTS9), SNP heritability about 5.13%, some replicated in a clinical cohort.
In 130 clinically defined UK patients, the first dedicated GWAS found a suggestive locus (rs1409440, OR 2.01, P 4x10-6) upstream of LHFPL6, replicated in 100,000 Genomes.
Preprint of the UK Lipoedema cohort GWAS: only suggestive loci, near lipoma formation, hormone biosynthesis and lipid hydroxylation genes.
Expert opinion (no quote available) describes lipedema as multifactorial on a polygenic predisposition.

propositions.statement_before_twin_merge: Genome-wide studies report common variant loci associated with a lipedema phenotype, suggesting a modest polygenic contribution.

propositions.statement: Rare variants in hormone-metabolism genes such as AKR1C1 have been reported in isolated lipedema families, but replication is lacking.
propositions.rationale: The only primary segregation evidence is one family (E24); reviews re-report it, and the PIT1 case is sporadic.

evidence.finding: Exome sequencing in one family found AKR1C1 p.L213Q in all 3 affected and none of 9 unaffected members, predicted to reduce 20alpha-HSD function.
Review cites AKR1C1 L213Q segregating across 3 generations, plus AKR1C2 Ser320PheTer2 and regulatory polymorphisms, proposing an AKR1C steroid-metabolism pathway.
Review re-reports the AKR1C1 mutation in a familial case and a PIT1 mutation in a sporadic case.

propositions.statement: Lipedema onset or worsening is frequently reported at female hormonal transitions, especially puberty, and also pregnancy and menopause.
propositions.rationale: Hormone-linked onset is context for how an inherited susceptibility may be expressed; primary onset data (E7, E9, E11, E15) are placed under the hereditary propositions where their main finding belongs. Same idea as G-00023, which the checker does not accept for this question, so stated as a new proposition with its wording.

evidence.finding: Review: lipedema almost exclusive to women, beginning in periods of hormonal change (puberty, pregnancy, menopause).
Review: onset thought to occur during hormonal fluctuation such as puberty, pregnancy or menopause.
Review emphasises estrogen: manifestation at hormonal change phases (puberty, pregnancy, menopause) and altered estrogen receptor alpha/beta distribution in adipose tissue.

propositions.statement_before_twin_merge: Lipedema onset or worsening is frequently reported at female hormonal transitions, especially puberty, and also pregnancy and menopause.

propositions.statement: Altered estrogen signalling in affected adipose tissue, including an imbalanced estrogen receptor pattern and local aromatase activity, is proposed as a lipedema mechanism.
propositions.rationale: These reviews propose estrogen-driven mechanisms, with genetic susceptibility as a possible component. Same idea as G-00025, which the checker does not accept for this question, so stated as a new proposition with its wording.

evidence.finding: Systematic review: lipedema appears multifactorial, driven mainly by hormonal (especially estrogen) dysregulation with metabolic and possibly genetic components.
Same systematic review conclusion (record title mismatched): hormonal dysregulation, especially estrogen, with metabolic and possibly genetic components.
Review: estrogen-regulated genetic predisposition with an altered ERalpha/ERbeta receptor pattern in white adipose tissue.

propositions.statement_before_twin_merge: Altered estrogen signalling in affected adipose tissue, including an imbalanced estrogen receptor pattern and local aromatase activity, is proposed as a lipedema mechanism.

propositions.statement: Starting hormonal contraception is reported by some women to coincide with lipedema symptom onset or worsening.
propositions.rationale: The case report's measured content is contraceptive-linked worsening; its family history is anecdotal. Same idea as G-00024, which the checker does not accept for this question, so stated as a new proposition with its wording.

evidence.finding: Case report: worsening swelling and pain after starting oral contraceptives at 24, partial improvement after stopping; family history of 'fat legs' mentioned anecdotally.

propositions.statement_before_twin_merge: Starting hormonal contraception is reported by some women to coincide with lipedema symptom onset or worsening.

dropped.reason: Mentions familial predisposition only in passing; heredity or family history not measured or tested.

verdicts.note: Primary surveys (E7, E9, E30, E14) show frequent but widely varying family history; E29/E26 correctly marked secondary of E11; E1 correctly context.

Hedged ('suggest', 'may'); E11 and E31 carry it, the restating reviews are correctly secondary. Mendelian framing sits in tension with the modest polygenic picture of P4 but the wording acknowledges alternative models.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Lipedema may be genetically heterogeneous, with candidate variants differing between affected families and no single shared causal gene identified.
verdicts.note: Rests on one small exome study (E19) plus its editorial; E24 (AKR1C1 family) and E12 (PIT1 in a sporadic case) also point to different genes in different families and could support it. Hedged with 'may', so minor.

E18 (UK Biobank, 18 loci, SNP heritability about 5%) and E15 (suggestive locus) support 'modest polygenic'; E16 correctly secondary of E15. Phenotype in E18 is inferred, not clinically diagnosed, but wording says 'lipedema phenotype'.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Rare variants in hormone-metabolism genes such as AKR1C1 have been reported in isolated lipedema families, with limited evidence beyond single families.
verdicts.note: 'Replication is lacking' is not stated in any item; E21 (no confirmed gene) is the closest. Reword to what the items show.

Statement is fine but only narrative reviews are cited. Primary data in the set are not placed here: E15 (cohort, onset frequently with hormonal change), E9 (puberty 49%, pregnancy 22%), E7 (onset clustered at adolescence), E14 (percent ranges), E22, E11 (onset at puberty in 55%).

verdicts.suggested_statement: Altered estrogen signalling in adipose tissue, including an imbalanced estrogen receptor pattern, is proposed as a lipedema mechanism and a possible link to heritable predisposition.
verdicts.note: Local aromatase activity appears in no finding placed here (it is in E22/E26, not listed); E4 and E3 state generic hormonal dysregulation, not receptor or aromatase mechanism, so they only partly support. E6, E17, E22, E26 describe the receptor/aromatase mechanism and should be placed here. Also only loosely about heredity.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Hormonal contraceptive use has been anecdotally linked to worsened lipedema symptoms, on very limited evidence.
verdicts.note: Single case report generalised to 'some women'; family history mention is not tied to this claim. Off-topic for heredity.

set_issues.issue: No proposition states the overall conclusion that a heritable component to lipedema is accepted (E1 Delphi consensus, E21/E26 genetic basis); E1 appears only as context under P1.
Primary onset data (E15, E9, E7, E14, E11) are not placed under P6, which cites only narrative reviews.
Mild tension between P2 (Mendelian autosomal dominant models) and P4/P3 (modest polygenic contribution, heterogeneity); the wording acknowledges both but does not reconcile them.
